r66 / 0.4.24 bounded source correction, 2026-10-18.

Failure attribution: root's approved 0.4.23 T183403Z run passed IPC/header checks, then Windows heartbeat atomic replacement hit sharing AccessDenied. The prior generic monitor mapping incorrectly called that lease resource loss, leading to an automatic second in-app generation. Root stopped and confirmed cleanup of both generations. Their existing logs/receipts are unchanged. This is integration I/O/fault classification, not model evidence.

Windows _write_json uses a unique UUID temp, atomic os.replace, and retries only WinError5/32/33. Linux atomic_json uses a unique UUID temp and only drvfs EACCES/EPERM/EBUSY/ETXTBSY. Backoff25ms doubling to200ms shares one 2-second monotonic deadline across write/replace/temp cleanup. Only the writer's own temp is unlinked; cleanup failure is retained as an exception note rather than deleting other files. Unexpected errors fail immediately. The original heartbeat payload's absolute expires_unix is unchanged during retries; expiry remains10seconds. Exhausted heartbeat writes are fatal xt_heartbeat_write_failed with errno/winerror/attempt count; Linux shared-file failures are fatal xt_monitor_failed with path/errno/attempt count and a stdout diagnostic if status itself cannot be published. No model, network request or generation retry was added.

Linux heartbeat reader preserves the previous successfully decoded same-token absolute deadline across transient missing/permission/busy or invalid-JSON reads. Read misses never renew it. A first heartbeat gets only a bounded2-second read window before any model can launch; there is no unvalidated cached lease. Wrong tokens or invalid expiry schemas are fatal. Windows status reader similarly retains the last valid same-token status; its existing15-second staleness window is measured from the original updated_unix (or initial run start before any status), so empty read results cannot evade stale detection. Status staleness is fatal xt_monitor_failed, not evidence of GPU lease preemption.

Only ViewEnded/LeasePreempted raised at the actual view.check boundary, with their event, map to xt_lease_ended. Existing explicit resource MovieFault and Linux real heartbeat-expiry/floor messages retain their classifications. All other monitor exceptions become fatal xt_monitor_failed. monitor-failure.json (or supervisor log if that write also fails) records the future failure. Fatal errors remain sticky through cleanup failures rather than becoming retryable resources.

Cleanup always continues to the existing owned targeted Linux cleanup even if stop.json cannot be written; it records that error and retains the lease until actual cleanup is confirmed. ensure cannot replace a failed live generation: it first cleans that manifest, and if release cannot be confirmed it returns fatal xt_previous_generation_unconfirmed with self._run retained. Root owns the separate coordinator retry allowlist/persisted3-reset cap. No fresh test was launched by this worker.

Implementation changed only relay/xt_services.py and vendor/linux_supervisor.py; r66 baselines and P14-shared-json-heartbeat.patch saved. Models/ports/deadlines/floor/private IPC/controller unchanged. Evidence: source reads/diffs/hashes only; no tests/imports/builds/apps/model runs. Runtime behavior still awaits a separately authorized run.

r67 approved small addendum: before any valid status, Windows uses xt_supervisor_first_status_seconds (default90, root validates30..120 and fingerprints it), measured from run.started_unix. Once last_valid_status is truthy, the unchanged15-second rule uses its original updated_unix. Both failures are fatal xt_monitor_failed with explicit phase first_status or stale plus age/limit. This permits cold WSL startup without changing the10-second actual heartbeat expiry or any model/load deadline. No runtime test performed.
